cohort: The study included 197 pregnant women between 28-42 weeks of gestation diagnosed with oligohydramnios (AFI < 5 cm).
finding: Oligohydramnios was significantly associated with adverse perinatal outcomes including abnormal fetal heart rate, meconium-stained fluid, low Apgar scores, NICU admissions, and a high perinatal mortality rate (22.7%).
mod_finding: Oligohydramnios was linked to a high rate of operative deliveries (86.6%), specifically higher cesarean section rates due to fetal distress.
cross-section timing: Observations were performed during the third trimester of pregnancy and around the time of birth to assess perinatal outcomes.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was observed in 10.9% of cases, but specific weight ranges for the cohort were not mentioned.
gest_age: 28-42 weeks (mean 37.12+/-2.59 weeks by LMP, 36.69+/-2.80 weeks by ultrasound)
